title: Psalm 113: The High God Who Stoops Low
summary: The servants of the LORD are called to praise his name at all times and in every place. He is exalted above the nations and the heavens, yet he stoops to look on the earth, lifts the poor from the dust to sit with princes, and gives the childless woman a home full of children.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 113
from.text: The psalm is a hymn of praise in three parts

line: The LORD is high above the nations, yet he stoops to lift the poor from the dust and gives the childless woman a home; the Hallel sung at the great festivals begins here.
guide: Ask where you look for greatness; God's is shown in how far down he reaches. Ask who is in the dust in your town, and whether you are willing to stoop with him.

care.text: A word of care. Verse 9 praises God for giving a child to a woman who had none. It does not promise a child to every woman who prays for one. Many faithful people long for children and never have them, or lose them before birth. Childlessness is not a judgment from God, and it does not measure your faith. Your longing is seen. If the grief is heavy, please share it with someone you trust: a friend, a pastor, a counsellor. The note on Psalms 127 and 128 says more.

stanzas.title: Praise the name of the LORD at all times and everywhere
Who is like the LORD, enthroned on high yet stooping low?
He lifts the poor and gives the barren a home

verses.t: Hallelujah! Give praise, O servants of the LORD; praise the name of the LORD.
Blessed be the name of the LORD both now and forevermore.
From where the sun rises to where it sets, the name of the LORD is praised.
The LORD is exalted over all the nations, His glory above the heavens.
Who is like the LORD our God, the One enthroned on high?
He humbles Himself to behold the heavens and the earth.
He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dump
to seat them with nobles, with the princes of His people.
He settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother to her children. Hallelujah!
